name: visidata
desc: Terminal spreadsheet multitool for discovering and arranging data
why: A terminal spreadsheet that can wander through unusual data shapes, plotting and pivoting with odd, discoverable depth.

brief.what_it_is: VisiData is a terminal spreadsheet-style interface for exploring and arranging tabular data. You point it at a file (vd <input>) or pipe command output into it (<command> | vd), and it opens an interactive grid. It reads a long list of formats, including CSV, TSV, JSON and JSON-Lines, SQLite, Excel, HDF5, Parquet-style tables, HTML, YAML, Markdown and git repositories according to the homepage, and it can compute Python for each row. Its homepage also advertises a batch mode (vd -b input.csv) for scripted pipelines, and Ctrl+Q quits.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes it as an open-source data multitool that combines the clarity of a spreadsheet, the efficiency of the terminal, and the power of Python in a lightweight utility that can handle millions of rows. The README frames it as a terminal interface for exploring and arranging tabular data.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. The homepage says it runs in Python and covers exploration, quick insights, cleaning data, instant histograms, terminal scatterplots, saved sessions for replay, and batch pipelines. The README notes that additional Python modules are needed for some formats.

brief.install_notes: Requires Python (the install page says 3.6+, the README says 3.8+). On macOS, use brew install visidata, pipx install visidata, or conda install --channel conda-forge visidata. Windows is not native: use WSL or MSYS2's Python. Linux packages exist for Debian, Fedora, NixOS, GNU Guix and Arch. Some formats need extra packages such as openpyxl and lxml, added with pipx --preinstall or pipx inject. Upgrade with pip install --upgrade visidata. If a format says 'package X not installed', confirm that vd and the package share an environment.
brief.standout: It handles a very wide range of formats and data shapes in one terminal tool, and it has built-in plotting (histograms, scatterplots) and Python-per-row computation. The README points to a deep set of discoverable commands (Ctrl+H opens a quick reference inside vd), which fits the 'odd, discoverable depth' idea.
brief.status: Maintained. The README header says v3.4, and the homepage lists v3.4 released Jun 30, 2026, after v3.3 (Sep 7, 2025), v3.2 (Jun 15, 2025) and v3.1 (Oct 14, 2024). The homepage blog has posts dated as recently as Mar 21, 2026. The GitHub README shows active CI badges and links to a Discord and an IRC channel for support.
brief.caveats: Windows is not supported natively and needs WSL or MSYS2. Python version requirements differ between the install page (3.6+) and the README (3.8+). Some formats need extra optional Python packages, and missing ones produce 'package X not installed' errors. The README warns that the develop branch installed from git may have intermittent issues. The stable code is GPLv3. The README notes that hundreds of commands and options exist beyond what it lists, so the docs are needed for depth. Maintenance is partly funded by Patreon and corporate sponsors.
